utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. This is Tuesday, September 8, 2009, and I would like to greet Mr. Praljak, as well as our accused, the Defence counsels, all the staff from the OTP. I also greet everyone helping us in our work. The Trial Chamber will now issue an oral decision regarding Vlado Sakic, an expert witness. Upon reading the latest witness schedule disclosed by the Praljak Defence on September 2, 2009, the Trial Chamber notes that the Praljak Defence planned to hear expert witness Vlado Sakic from October 5 to October 7, 2009, and to examine the witness for two hours and 30 minutes. However, in its order of May 6, 2009, on the capacity and the modalities governing the hearing of Vlado Sakic, expert witness, the Trial Chamber gave the Praljak Defence two hours for its examination-in-chief and for possible redirect regarding expert witness Vlado Sakic. Given the time granted to the Praljak Defence, the Trial Chamber gave two hours to the Prosecution and one hour altogether to the other Defences for the cross-examination of expert witness Vlado Sakic. Consequently, the Trial Chamber reminds the Praljak Defence that it will have two hours and that two hours and 30 minutes for its examination-in-chief and possible redirect regarding expert witness Vlado Sakic. Very well. In a nutshell, when this witness will come, this expert witness will come, the Praljak Defence will have two hours for the examination-in-chief. Furthermore, yesterday the Trial Chamber had been seized of two motions made by Mrs. Alaburic to have five minutes -- five additional minutes to put questions in the framework of a possible cross-examination of Mr. Praljak, and Ms. Nozica also told us that she might need 15 additional minutes to put questions as cross-examination questions. The Trial Chamber grants these motions; however, the time used by the Petkovic and the Stojic Defence will be deducted from the time they have been allotted for their case. Mr. Stringer, you have the floor. I know you want to take the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, if the floor is to restart cross-examination, we did have a short application on our side. It was notified to Your Honours, we thought. Your Honours, this application on behalf of the Petkovic and the Praljak Defences, and Your Honours will recall that you directed that a written motion should be filed in relation to disclosure under Rule 68. We're on the verge of filing that motion, Your Honour, but we're just running into slight difficulty on the word limit, and the application is to have the word limit extended from the normal 3.000 to 3.500 words. We want to go into enough detail about the sort of material we're looking for to make it a helpful and manageable motion. So, Your Honour, our application is very simple on behalf those two Defences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me consult with my fellow Judges. Obviously we all agree. The Trial Chamber agrees, and you can use 3.500 words, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President, Your Honours, counsel, and everyone else in and around the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, General.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And, General, before I begin or continue with the cross-examination --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I just wanted to take the floor to make one clarification for the record from yesterday. When we were talking about the TV ORF video which was one of the video-clips we looked at on the bridge, and it's the clip that there appears to have been some sort of a splice or alteration. And in the course of the discussion I note some comments were made, and I don't know, maybe it's just my own sensitivity, but I don't know whether there was an impression created that that video that appears to have been spliced originates from the Office of the Prosecutor. And I just wanted to make it clear from the record that the TV ORF video based on the testimony of Professor Jankovic when he testified on the 30th of June last year, testified that he was provided with the TV ORF video along with the TV Mostar video, that he used those to prepare his report and that he received those from the Praljak Defence. And so just for the record, I wanted it to be clear that those are -- at least the TV ORF video does not originate from the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: General, when we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Stringer, this goes without saying, what you just said. Of course the video had been disclosed by the Praljak Defence to Professor Jankovic, and we had understood that the OTP had nothing to do with this video in the first place, had nothing to do with making this video in the first place. It was really obvious for us. It went without saying, but you wanted to say this on the transcript so much the better.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Mr. Stringer, Mr. Jankovic and I did not have at our disposal the tape in its entirety as you showed it yesterday. It wasn't broadcast that way. We only had the video that was broadcast; whereas, this one here is a broader version, the one we saw yesterday. It's longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just for the record, to make it quite clear, Dr. Jankovic, the expert witness, very precisely in his report and in testifying here explained the origins and source of the two videotapes that he used. They were videotapes as they were broadcast on the two mentioned television networks and nothing more than that. I didn't hear what was said very well. We didn't say that the Prosecutor acquired it. We explained what the source was and where the videotapes had come from, so there's no misunderstanding or dispute there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The only problem left comes from what Mr. Praljak just told us. He told us that yesterday when he was watching the video with everyone else, he noted that the entire sequence we saw yesterday is not the same sequence as the one that he himself, that his counsel and Professor Jankovic had seen. According to him, this video is longer. The Trial Chamber will reflect on this, think about it. I wanted to put something on the transcript yesterday. I forgot to do it, so I'll do it now. I must say that I saw -- if someone saw the same thing please tell us, but we saw this waterfall. We saw a cloud of smoke or dust, then we saw a white stone falling from the bridge into the Neretva, and there was a splash right after that, and then for several minutes after that we saw the cloud that was clearing up with time, but the bridge was still standing for a good number of minutes after we saw the first waterfall. Then we saw an image where the bridge collapsed into the river. That's what we saw. And I believe we all saw the same thing. If someone didn't see that, please say so, but this is what we saw yesterday. Now, given what Mr. Praljak just told us, we have a new problem: The time spent between the waterfall, the cloud of dust or smoke, and the collapse, it seems to be different. He's telling us that we saw a different video than the one that he, his counsel, and his expert saw when they were drafting the report of Professor Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, just for the record, I think the video you're referring to now, the one in which the bridge is still standing, is -- is from Exhibit P01040, 1040. And just for the record, 1040 - because this came up yesterday as well - 1040 is a compilation. It's a long video, and so the part that we're focussed on now on this part is just one part of it. The video has lots of different things on it, but I think that the President's just now made reference to Exhibit P1040. I don't know we can resolve this any more today, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I remember that the Prosecution informed the Chamber and the others in the courtroom what was the source of that video shooting the Prosecutor showed us yesterday, which is P1040. We don't know the source. The Prosecutor is practically testifying about that. For the Defence, the Defence brought an expert to testify about that. Now we have the Prosecution testimony. We don't know the source of that video and whether that is the same one or it is not the same one as it was presented by witness expert. I think that the Prosecution should show where that video is coming from, because even in the e-court it has a wrong date. It is, what, 11 months -- it is 11 months before actually the bridge fall, and this is at least something which nobody dispute, the date of the fall of the bridge. So I would kindly request the Prosecution to give us the source. We can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stringer, this P -- the video P01040, could you tell us what its source is?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I can't give you the source at this moment. I know that it was disclosed to the Defence on the 19th of January, 2005. I'm pretty confident that it was among the exhibits that we used in our cross-examination of Professor Jankovic, and if that's the case, the source would have been indicated on the list that would have been in the binder that went out to all the parties before we began our cross-examination, because we generally include the source of all the cross-examination exhibits. So I think that with a little bit of diligence any of us could determine the source based upon what's been provided in the past, but certainly we'll look at -- into it and see if we can remind everybody what the source is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm really sorry, but maybe it's better to clear these things completely. As my dear colleague said, and I agree with that, a video under this number was presented to [indiscernible] Professor Jankovic who was here in the courtroom. So we do have his answers, his responses to that question on the record. So there is no need to discuss that. We agree whatever the expert said. We are fine. But another thing, the Prosecution, my dear colleague, just said that this material was disclosed long ago to the Defence, and yes, indeed, we agree with that; but the problem of the source remain, because as the Prosecutor said, this video is compilation of many other images from Mostar and area. It is compilation, and I stress that word, this is compilation. We don't know who did it, how, when, et cetera. Now, what I am interested is to know exactly where this part of this big compilation, the part about the bridge which we saw yesterday, 1040, a part of evidence 1040, where this particular shot came from. Who is the author, when?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacic, if you look at the transcript, on 1st of July, 2008, at page 30170, line 50 -- 15 or something, I find that Ms. West told the Chamber that this exhibit was tendered into evidence by Witness Denis Saric. Now, do you challenge that? I think you could have looked it up and find it. I have the fearing that we are a bit losing time right now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, that's another tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think that we are talking about the same, the evidence. The cite is witness Delalic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: But the number here is 01040.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I cannot claim now. It could be some -- it could be some mistake, but I'm also looking in history at that document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Well, may I suggest that before we lose time on such discussions in the courtroom, time which is very scarce, this be prepared beforehand and then a precise motion be made in this respect. I don't think it is helpful just raising questions of, I don't know, and this and that when there is some material in our transcript, and it seems not to really have been looked at and properly examined before. I think we should let Mr. Stringer start now with the --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: But I --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. It's not that I'm challenging the transcript. What is in the transcript is in the transcript, certainly. I merely wanted to correct you that in the -- what you said, at least what is written in the transcript now is that it was Witness Denis Saric, Saric. There was no such witness. According to the history in the e-court, the witness was Delalic, Enes Delalic. So I --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So I referred to this confusion. And I'm now not going into assume, rightly said, I'm now not going to improvise, but Delalic brought another video which we also saw yesterday or day before yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But anyway, my point is only that we should know the source. The Prosecutor is using it. He should say, This is shot by this and this man on this and that day and have to document that on some way. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President. Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Denis Saric is a 92 bis witness. All right? So there is a witness Denis Saric. He's the source of the tape and that's what Ms. West referred to. We can line all this up for Mr. Kovacic, and we'll provide him with all of the details after the next break. That's my proposal, rather than taking more court time on this now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I just wanted to say that it is in -- all my discussion is based on what I can see from e-court document. In description of e-court, it is not as the Prosecutor said. It is Delalic, and it is another day. So if there is any mistake, I cannot be blamed for that. Sorry. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kovacic, the Trial Chamber admitted a document, P1040. The Legal Officer told me that this document had been admitted when witness Delalic was heard. When witness Delalic came to testify, we played the video and the Trial Chamber admitted Exhibit P1040. It seems now that this video was actually shot by witness Denis Saric, a 92 bis witness. He is the person who gave this video to the OTP. Now you have it. It's a bit complex, but I believe it's clear now. It's clear, because now you have all the elements.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: With all due respect, Your Honour, I think that somebody -- there is some mistake. Saric took --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, I object to further interventions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: -- the video which was shown by the Prosecutor before 1040, one we were looking at yesterday, the one where nothing is seen. So there must be some error or some confusion. I don't know what is it. I cannot tell you now. Somebody should -- should investigate, but this is simply not correct. This is --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, the last time I spoke I said that we would look into it and provide Mr. Kovacic with the information he requires over the break. We're just beating a dead horse. Let's just move on to the cross-examination. We'll provide him the information he wants --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stringer, rest assured you will be able to finish your cross-examination. Please prepare all the information for Mr. Kovacic and hand it over to him and we'll come back to this, I'm sure, at one point in time. As you know, the Trial Chamber is still waiting for the conclusions of the witness, expert witness. Mr. Stringer, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: General, yesterday I believe we were leaving off with -- or discussing P09817. I had pretty much completed my questions to you about that document. This was from 29 October 1993, and I won't re-read the document, and we all recall what you said about it, it relates to some coordination issues between the HVO and the VRS in the Vares area. Related to this, I believe, is the next document, which I would like to ask you about, P06219. Now, this one, General, is -- it's dated the same day. It appears to be dated the same day, 29 October. And now this is Rajic reporting to a number of different individuals and bodies, Mr. Stojic, yourself, General Petkovic, and here we see that Rajic is reporting that: "The XY side is not implementing any part of the agreement between General Petkovic and General Milovanovic." And then moving to the next paragraph Rajic says: "It is necessary to urgently establish contact between Mr. Stojic and Mr. Kovacevic in order to get this going so that assistance can be provided to Vares." General, first of all, do you know what is the agreement between General Petkovic and General Milovanovic that is refer to here by Colonel Rajic?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone for the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what Mr. Petkovic agreed with Mr. Milovanovic because I wasn't present at the meeting, and I don't remember that we discussed it later on when Petkovic returned, but most probably it was some form of, as you say, co-operation or some form of payment for assistance for treatment, something of that nature, and for the procurement, perhaps, of some weapons or ammunition to defend Vares.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know who General Milovanovic is?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And here the reference to urgently establishing contact, or he says: "It is necessary to urgently establish contact between Mr. Stojic and Mr. Kovacevic ..." Do you know who Mr. Kovacevic is that's referred to here?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know whether Mr. Stojic had meetings with any of his counterparts on the VRS side in respect of co-operation issues?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I assume so, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. And -- well, let's stay with this issue. I've got one more document on this topic, and the next exhibit is P06364. And this is just now a few days later, now the 2nd of November, 1993, and this is Rajic reporting to Mr. Stojic in the Ministry of Defence on the equipment received from the XY side and per request, and this then contains a list of the various MTS that according to Rajic has been received from the XY side. General, you just said that you assumed that Stojic had meetings with counterparts in the VRS. Based on Mr. Stojic's role in procuring MTS, is that a topic that Mr. Stojic would have been dealing with with the VRS people?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer, I said probably, and probably that was the topic. So I can confirm only that, that I sought and approved talks in order to be able to obtain some materiel and equipment for this area to be defended against the BH Army attacks, but I didn't know whether they really met, how they paid, where they met, whether they met at all. It would be too much to ask from me. Well, I'm talking about myself. I asked for those talks to be conducted.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. Then that would suggest, General, that in efforts to obtain MTS from the Serb side, the VRS, Mr. Stojic's role would have been in sort of a logistics and possibly the financial aspects of that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could conclude that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: General, the next exhibit -- oh.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to come back to this document. First of all, in November, specifically November 2nd, did you know in your capacity as commander of the HVO that the Serb side was supplying military equipment, namely weapons, and two tanks, there are two tanks, one is clearly not in running order, is obsolete. Did you know this?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indiscernible]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good. So you did know it. So let us try to step back now. And here I'm not speaking to you in your capacity as General, I'm speaking to you as a person who was at one point a deputy minister of defence in the Croat Republic and who understands the issues at hand. How do you explain this politically speaking, in political terms, at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was difficult for one very simple reason, and that is that you cannot, as commander of an army, leave the wounded people untreated, and you cannot allow anybody who is attacking you to take some territory, expel the people, if you have any means at your disposal to obtain at a very high price the necessary materiel and equipment that might prevent it. So I still maintain what I said before. They started that before, and I approved it. I wasn't aware of the quantities, however. So from the political point of view it was very complicated, but at that time I was the commander of the Main Staff, and the United Nations did not label the Army of Republika Srpska as a criminal organisation, a crime syndicate which would prevent me from obtaining from them weapons in order to defend myself, to defend an area that was under attack and to help the HVO that was defending it. I could have gone to anywhere else in Europe to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask a slightly more complicated question. We have a document which contains a list of the equipment. At first glance this is costly, tanks, mortars, and so on. This costs money. You have said that as far as payment is concerned it may be the Department of Defence that will implement payment even though we know, because we heard several witnesses speak to this, we know that there was a prepared annual budget at the time for Herceg-Bosna, so that this was something that had to be factored into the budget. This is not what I intend to address with my question. If the XY side, the Serbs, are to supply or were to supply this equipment, does this mean that in terms of Republika Srpska, at this highest level, Karadzic, Mladic, were informed of this, or was this done behind their back by corrupt military officers who, behind the backs of the politicians, were engaging in this type of arms trafficking?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I cannot answer that question. I know that -- well, I remember well that the prices were extremely, enormously high and that as far as I know, at least 80 per cent of the costs for the treatment and procurement was paid by the people from the Vares municipality. They collected the money in all kinds of ways, from abroad and so on. And I think that we had a witness who testified here and who explained how and to whom they took the money and who was aware of it on the Republika Srpska Army side, and how high it went. I really don't have any facts that I could share with you now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understood, if I am not mistaken, that you said that during this period, July, August, September, October, you had remained on the front because there was a front that was 200 kilometres long, fighting was taking place, and you were truly in the front line facing the enemy. I understood through what you have said and I drew the conclusion that at times you were squaring off or facing off with the Serbs and sometimes with the Muslims because the front was fairly long. I can concluded -- I can conclude that during this period from July to October at times there was some fighting with the Serb side. Can you confirm that during this period there was fighting with Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we find ourselves in the very extraordinary situation, and it may be the first time that has been seen in the history of war where the belligerent parties are passing, either directly or indirectly, weapons. For example, tanks. We have two tanks, one of which is in operating order. What does that mean? The tank is taken, it's put in position, and one shoots at the Serbs. In other words, one is shooting at those who procured the tank or who ceded the tank. Is that possible, or is that completely unthinkable, inconceivable?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. First of all, it all started in October, not before that. When the BH Army launched its offensive on Vares, that's when it started. That's when the co-operation started as an effort in the defence, this effort to procure the weapons. As they were isolated and the tanks, one of them was out of order, the other one was functioning, they could defend the territory only against the BH Army. Well, I couldn't have used it in any way to fight the Serbs, that specific tank. Other tanks were used, but not that one. The situation, Your Honours, was very complicated if you take into account the fact that in the Bihac area the Muslim army of Fikret Abdic fought at the BH Army. Unfortunately, every part of Bosnia and Herzegovina had its own specificities and peculiarities and those problems had to be solved at the level -- at the local level, and globally there were always attempts to reach peace between the BH Army and the HVO in areas where the BH Army was attacking, because more than ten full-strength HVO brigades were fighting at the very same time together with the BH Army against the Republika Srpska Army under the BH Army command. I drew all that on the map when we had the former member of the BH Presidency, Mr. Kljujic, here. I can list them for you: Sarajevo, Tuzla, Usora, Posavina, Bihac, and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Just one follow-up question on that, General. During the time that you were commander of the HVO Main Staff, or at any time were you aware that General Mladic with the VRS had to personally approve the movement of HVO personnel through VRS-held territory?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't have any such information. On several occasions approval was granted for the movement of those HVO troops and the people who lost the fight, such as, for instance, in Travnik, and they were retreating through the territory controlled by the VRS, the Republika Srpska Army. And then after Bugojno, a good part of the people and of the troops again had to flee in the face of the aggression by the BH Army through -- or, rather, they fled to the Serbs, sort to speak. And then some talks were held and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation] The document that we see on weapons shows -- the document on weapons shows that there is co-operation. Some may wonder why bother insisting or dwelling on this question, but when one knows all of the case, one may wonder when the Ivica Rajic conducts the operation in Stupni Do, and they require the authorisation of the Serb side to go through the territory. At that time, authorisation is given to go through the territory because there already is a form of co-operation as concerns weapons, and Ivica Rajic who knows a lot about this, as the document is from him, when he asks the Serb side to get authorisation to go through the territory to reach Stupni Do, the Serb side -- the Serb side says, "Yes. Go ahead." What do you think of this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is true that Ivica Rajic travelling from Kiseljak to Vares had to pass through the territory controlled by the VRS, as far as I know, but this co-operation was not co-operation like you would have among friends. Everything was paid for. So it was a market thing. Well, even -- it was higher than the market price, in fact. And secondly, it was in the interest of the Serb side for the Croats in Vares to fight their enemy, because -- and that's why they assisted by letting the HVO soldiers through to die there, because once Vares fell, they were the next in line for an attack. So it was a very logical, pragmatic military situation. So you always have to give another side to fight your enemy, and the BH Army was their enemy. It was quite clear as it was to us, but unfortunately you had two interested parties here, the HVO. It was in my interest as the commander for Vares not to fall, and the Serbs had the same interest. They didn't want me to lose this position. I didn't want to lose the position, because people would have to flee, and they had a different interest. If Vares fell, then the BH Army Corps would attack them. They were the first in line for an attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: General, I want to move on to the next topic here. We have not talked about the use of the Muslim prisoners for forced labour, and I want to take you to Exhibit P06937. It should be the next document in your binder. And I know, General, that you claim -- you said this on the 23rd of June here. You claim that this document does not bear your signature and that it is a false document, at least to the extent it indicates that you approved of the taking away of these 40 prisoners from the Heliodrom on the 8th of November, 1993. Do I correctly understand your testimony on that, General?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer. This is a clear-cut forgery. I never ever approved the taking out of prisoners --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So you --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- anywhere, prisoners that were taken to do some work then.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So you're saying you did not approve someone else to put your signature on this document for you?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I claim that this is a clear cut forgery that was produced for I don't know what reason. On the 8th of November, they were taken out and I was not there at all, and I claim that this was a forgery, that somebody simply forged the signature, took it from somewhere. General Slobodan Praljak, well, there's always something typewritten. This is a forgery. This was copied from another document with another stamp. Well, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: General, can we agree that this document bears two stamps? The first stamp, the upper stamp, being the stamp of the military police next to the name of Mijo Jelic, and then the stamp underneath that is the stamp of the HVO Main Staff; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So that if this was forged, General, you claim it was forged by someone in your own Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, it's impossible to forge my signature in the Main Staff. I don't know who forged it. I simply know that unfortunately earlier on regarding the trial and the Tribunal lots of services were trying to fabricate documents that actually had not existed at the time of the events --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: General --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- but were produced later on and I don't want to speculate now who it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So you're suggesting that the document may have been prepared sometime after the 8th of November, 1993. Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I don't want to say when this document was drafted. I simply want to say that this document or any document of a similar kind was never signed by me, ever. And secondly, on the 8th of November, which is the time in question, I was not in Citluk. I was not in the Main Staff. As other evidence will show, I came later, and I don't know in what period this was done. I'm talking only about my signature, when these elements that concern me, were added to this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. General, now, to stay with this specific order, I want to take you to the next exhibit, P02642, 2642. And, General, this is a log-book referencing orders for the release of POWs to work, and I'd like to direct your attention, General, to item 407 in this log-book, which in your version is on the page ending with the number 7502. Page 17 of the English, item 407. So, General, we can go back and look at the previous document, the order itself, and the order bears the file number 02-717/93, and indeed, General, what we see in this log-book now is a specific reference to this order among lots of other orders that are contained in this book. So, General, the fact is that whoever allegedly forged this order on taking the prisoners to work would also have had to somehow modify or forge the HVO's own logbooks setting out all the orders for prisoners to work; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. This is -- I don't know when this log-book was created. It's the log-book of the military police administration, and it is quite probable that somebody brought this order of this kind here and then just made the entry, the appropriate entry, but this has nothing to do with it. On that day, I was not in the Main Staff at the relevant time, and in the 422 or 500 -- well, on the 8th -- on the 8th when I was not there, somebody planted this one on me. No, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. And whoever did that had access to the Main Staff's stamp that they used to affix the stamp onto the order itself. So, General, for us to believe your story, we have to believe that this happened from inside the Main Staff on or about the 8th of November, 1993; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true. When something is forged -- well, I kept asking myself why there's this number 2 and not 1 on this stamp. We discussed it. Well, it's easy to copy the stamp, and it's easy to copy my signature. Somebody simply took the Main Staff stamp with number 2 from some other document. I really don't know what that means. I don't it, but I was not at that time there, and I did not sign any such approvals ever.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I've finished my questions on this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, I told you I would have a few questions on the maps. Before we begin with the maps --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. President. I've finished with this couple of documents. I still got a little more cross-examination left. I apologise. I didn't know if the Trial Chamber had any questions on this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry. I thought you were finished. Please then go ahead, and I shall return to this later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: General, I just wanted to pass back a bit to an issue we discussed a bit at an earlier part in your cross-examination, although I think I failed to get our record clear enough on it, so I want to come back, and this relates to the Convicts Battalion and its status in respect of the HVO, and so I want to take you back to the chart that you made when you testified in the Naletilic case, Exhibit P09324, and also the transcript of your testimony in that case, which we've marked as an exhibit here as P10980. So this is in Sanction so that we can put it up, the transcript on, on everybody's screens. General, I just want to read from two pages of your testimony in the Naletilic case when you were talking about this chart and making your markings on, and this is at page 9573 of the Naletilic transcript. I'm going to begin on line 21 where Mr. Seric begins taking. Mr. Seric was the lawyer at the time for Vinko Martinovic and he says: "Mr. President, since the title says that this is the diagram of the HVO structure from 1993, and we have the witness's precise answer when that was, I think it would be fair to him to also put the date next to this box, the date when he assumed his duty." And then Mr. Scott said: "I agree with that. " And then the Presiding Judge, Judge Liu, agreed. So then Mr. Scott asked you, General, the following, this is line 4 of the next page: "All right, sir. Thank you. That's exactly why I'm asking you to look at this chart, to avoid confusion, because in the box it says 'supreme commander.' But that may have been misinterpreted to be chief commander, or whatever you -- Chief of the Main Staff. So when in this chart it says 'supreme commander,' as of the date you've now written, the 27th of July, 1993, who was that?" And, General, your answer is: "Mr. Mate Boban." And then we see you write that on the chart. And we can see you're writing on the chart as we're looking at the exhibit now. And then you're asked by Mr. Scott: "And as of July 27, 1993, what was the -- whatever term you want, minister or secretary of the Defence Department?" And your answer: "Mr. Bruno Stojic." Mr. Scott asked you to please write that on the chart, which you do. Then Mr. Scott says: "Now, can you tell us, please, looking at this chart, can you tell us where the Convicts Battalion fits on this chart?" And the transcript tells us that you indicate, you point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT SAYS
utterances.text: "Can you mark that, please? Why don't you put K -- well, you can put whatever you like. I suggest you might put KB." And then you marked on the chart. Now, I'm going to stop there. Mr. Scott goes on to ask you about Mladen Naletilic and where he would appear on the chart, and I'm not interested in that today, General. I just want you to confirm for us, please, that when you wrote KB on the chart here, P09324, you were making reference to the Convicts Battalion as of the 27th of July, 1993.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- the time that I was asked that, at that time the Convicts Battalion, at that time -- well, it's how I said it. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, General, I'm ready to move to the last exhibit of this cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: May I -- sorry, I think the record is not entirely clear. The answer was not quite clear. The question, I think, refers to the 27th of July, 1993, and the answer says: "At the time, well, it's -- the time that I was asked that." And the time that the witness was asked that was the time of the hearing in the Tuta-Stela case. So I want you to be precise. Mr. Praljak, you affirm that the organisation as indicated on document P09324 was that which prevailed on 27th of July, 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Judge Trechsel, Your Honour. I wouldn't put it that way. It's -- well, I came in to testify about something quite different, and then somebody put this. Now, when I look at the special purpose units, they're placed in the same box as the professional units. Now, professional units, of course, were units under the command of the Main Staff, but not all of them. So this kind of examination with suggestions and so on, I'm not going to go back on my words, but I'm not going to testify and say that I had time -- or, rather, if I had time to draw a diagram of what the whole set-up looked like from the main command and staff, no, I'm not going to do that or say that. What I was asked was: Is Mate Boban the supreme commander. Yes, he is. And was Mr. Bruno Stojic the head of the Defence Department at the time? Yes. Where was the ATG? It was in the Special Purpose area, and I wasn't asked anything more than that. So that's it. Whether the certain units -- Special Purpose Units were separate and who commanded them and who commanded the professional units, there weren't questions of that kind and so everything remains masked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I would rather like to unmask, Mr. Praljak. When you said Naletilic -- no, not the -- the Kinder Battalion -- the Convicts Battalion belonged to those special units, you were referring to a specific moment in time, namely the 27th of July, 1993? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To the best of my knowledge, at the time I was convinced that had it existed and that it belonged somewhere. Now, as I had and didn't want to have anything to do about with that man or anything he was in charge of after that time, then I can say in quite precise terms that he wasn't under my command. Now, who's command he was under --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Once again, Mr. Praljak, would you be so kind as to answer my question? I have not asked you whether he was under your command. Maybe I must understand you as saying that you simply do not remember what you were saying then and what you meant when you were answering the question of Mr. Scott in Tuta-Stela with regard to this Kinder Battalion. Is that what I must understand? You don't know any more whether you were saying that this was the situation on the 27th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. STINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Judge, I apologise for interrupting, but again you said Kinder Battalion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Ah, I'm sorry, thank you, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And that's a different unit that needs to be distinguished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Ah, yes. Convict. Convict. I find it difficult to put the K at the head of convict.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Praljak, I was listening to Mr. -- my fellow Judge, Mr. Stringer, and my -- and your answers, but I was also looking at the very professional questions put to you by Mr. Scott during that -- during his examination. Very professional. He was asking you very specific question, and you were to answer him, and you answer him. And on this document that we all have here on the screen, you know, he asked you to mark a number things, which you do. But then on page 9574, line 24 I note the following: Mr. Scott, in a very professional fashion, is asking you questions on Mladen Naletilic. You were a witness in the Naletilic case, and he is asking you where Naletilic fits in on this organisational chart. That's the question he is putting to you at the time. Theoretically, since you already answered all his questions, you were probably going to put Naletilic some place in the organisational chart, but this is your answer. You're saying, Mladen Naletilic, Tuta, was not the commander of the Convicts Battalion, and I don't really know where he fits in in this organisational chart. In a nutshell, that's your answer. So we have a very specific question put by Mr. Scott on Naletilic, and we have a very specific answer from you. According to you, Tuta was not the commander, and since he was not commanding the battalion, he cannot be placed in this organisational chart. Do you remember this answer that you had put to -- that you had given Mr. Scott? I mean, it's noted on the transcript, but I want to make sure that you remember what you said at the time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's quite certainly what my answer was, Your Honours. However, if I was to answer that question today, I would say that according to my information, that most probably that's where it was. Now, this Convicts Battalion, when it took part in the liberation of Mostar, Tuta -- Tuta wasn't the commander. I don't want to justify myself or say that there was even a single little lie, but maybe I wasn't precise enough. Of course, with the best intentions in mind. What I remember, or, rather, I knew at the time that he wasn't the commander of what was then called the Convicts Battalion, although they called themselves the Tutic's men, the Convicts, whatever, and some other names they used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So at the time either you were telling the truth or you were lying, but you were under oath. So I assume you were telling the truth. If Naletilic had been the commander of the KB, would you have marked under KB something? You know, maybe a circle with "Tuta" written in it or something. If he had been the commander of the KB, would you have marked the document in that fashion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wasn't lying then, and I'm not lying now, not at all. I would have written in that the Convicts Battalion existed and most probably Tuta was in command. I would also sign and say that it wasn't under the Main Staff. That is what I would sign up to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You answer Mr. Scott by saying that the commander was not Naletilic. He maybe should have asked you who was the commander then if it wasn't Naletilic. I'm putting it to you now. Who was the commander of the Convicts Battalion at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, the time 1992 when the Convicts Battalion was under the command of Andabak, that's when I said Tuta wasn't the commander. I sort of reduced the time. I don't know who was the commander at the time, and this was a year later. So I seem to join two facts. When Andabak was the commander of the Convicts Battalion, when I agreed on the operation at Orlovac with him, and I seemed to have put the two things together. And I also made a mistake. I exaggerated to Mr. Scott when I said that I came on the 27th. I came on the 24th. 1993, that is. Now, there are always possible mistakes can make but not lies. Lies do not exist. They is imprecisions in the time periods and time frames and time perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this organisational chart that we have here on the screen which is marked by you, well, we shouldn't read the September -- we shouldn't read 27/07, we should read the 24/07. The supreme commander is Mate Boban and then there's Bruno Stojic, and then you take your post as the HVO -- chief of the HVO Main Staff, and regarding the Convicts Battalion, you have no idea who the commander was. You know that in 1992 it was Andabak but on July 24th you have no idea who the person might be. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right. That's quite right. Yes. So it should be corrected to read the 24th and everything else is as you have put it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: General, again as I indicated, for purposes of this discussion I'm not interested in who the commander of the Convicts Battalion was or who you think it was or whether you know who it was. Can we agree to this, General: That on the -- on Friday, the 5th of April, 2002, when you were sitting at that very spot in this courtroom, testifying under oath, that you wrote KB in this place on this chart? Can we agree to that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with that. I agree that I put that in at the time that you stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'm ready to move to my final document, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: General, on the 14th of July of this year you were being asked questions about the presence of members of the Croatian Army within the ranks of the HVO, and I was asking you about the southern front, and we were looking at a document, P03667, which is not in the binder. It's the one that had a reference to parents protesting their children being sent to the southern front, and on page 43015 of the transcript you said, line 2: "It says here that there were spontaneous rallies and protests, but I repeat, nobody came to the HVO to fight without being a volunteer. As I've already said several times and I've shown you in the documents, they could possibly refuse an order of that kind without any military consequences." Now, General, I want you to look at P11033, because I'm going to challenge that assertion that you made in your testimony with this document, and you will recall earlier on your cross-examination that we were looking at various documents from Brigadier Kapular of the Croatian Army. General, this is the 27th of November, 1993. So this is shortly after you resigned the position as commander of the HVO. After a long list of names of members of the 4th Motorised Brigade, Commander Kapular, this document says, they bear responsibility for refusing to obey the order on marching of the unit to the southern front on the 2nd October 1993 and 11th November 1993 as members of the 4th Motorised Brigade. It goes on to say that all of these people are going to have disciplinary measure of a 20 per cent salary reduction over three months based on their refusal to obey the order. And it goes on to discuss some additional people for whom disciplinary measures are not imposed. And then the document continues on with a section, this is page 3 of the English, of a statement of reasons, and in the fourth paragraph under the statement of reasons Kapular writes: "One of the basic duties of the guardsmen is to perform all tasks without questioning them, scrupulously, independently, efficaciously and professionally, as well as to be ready for personal sacrifices and professional risks, so I consider that in the concrete case there was no place for subjective attitude towards the order that was the subject matter of the disciplinary violations ..." So, General, what that tells us is that on these two relevant dates, the 2nd of October, 1993, and the 11th of November, these members of the 4th Motorised Brigade, or at some point shortly before, these members, these HV soldiers, received an order to go to the southern front; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the HV, not the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, the fact is, General, that the -- "southern front" was the terminology used within the HV in order to send its personnel down into Bosnia-Herzegovina so that it could regulate their status as HV members who were part of the HVO. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the way you're saying it. The southern front was the southern front of the Croatian Army, and it included territory from Split to the south, Prevlaka and Dubrovnik. And it's also correct that the volunteers, through -- being sent through the southern front secured what I was talking about; however, in this document, in no way is there any mention as to why and how and where those people were sent.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Let me --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please. It doesn't say that anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to put to you that what this tells us is that we have these individuals who were, in fact, ordered to go down to fight with the HVO in Bosnia-Herzegovina. They refused to do so, and that despite what you've said in your testimony, they did suffer consequences as a result of that refusal. Isn't that really how it was?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not. I don't see any possibility of a commander of the 5th Guards Brigade, Ivan Kapular, to issue an order to people from the 4th Guards Brigade and to punish the members of the 4th Guards Brigade. And I simply don't see that anywhere. It doesn't say anywhere that they left and how can he be in control and command the 4th Guards Brigade which is in Split whereas he's in Vinkovci 3, 4, 500 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, General, the fact is that the southern front was HVO in BiH and that these individuals were ordered to go, not volunteers; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct. It is incorrect, and you can't see that and say that from any of the documents here. Why they didn't carry something out, you can't see that from this document. And I claim that nobody was punished because they were all volunteers. So nobody suffered any consequences.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President. This completes our cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's have a break. We will reconvene in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, over the break we've prepared a cheat sheet or just something that we think sets out the history in terms of that videotape that was being discussed at the beginning, and so if we could distribute this around. We gave one to your court officer, but then since then we had one correction to make on something, so we can do this now or we can just do it outside the courtroom and everybody can go away and look at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber obtained this document, the document that you also gave to all Defence teams, and when we read this document, we note that this video was handed over to you by Witness Saric. That goes without saying. However, your document does not say who actually shot the scene, who put it on camera. We don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think that information is contained in the Rule 92 bis statement by Mr. Saric, and that's in -- in fact, I don't know, does the Defence have this, because I can give it to the Registrar and we can pass it around. In the third paragraph, this is part of when Mr. Flynn was explaining the video. And in his 92 bis statement, Saric said, "I'm handing over to you a one-and-a-half-hour video cassette that I personally recorded of different programmes broadcast by the Croatian HTV in Mostar in 1993. In the recordings, there are a view of the Mostar Bridge before the war and when it was destroyed. So, Mr. President, the answer in terms of who recorded it is contained in the 92 bis statement of Mr. Saric, which is Exhibit Number P10143.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So in Mr. Saric, in his 92 bis statement hands over to the OTP a video cassette which is an hour and a half long, saying that this was recorded from HTV, Croat television in Mostar, in 1993. That's all we have; right? Is that it? Mr. Stringer should answer. [In English] It's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: That's correct. And just for the record, Mr. Saric did not testify in the trial as a viva voce witness. He appeared only via rule 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, you wanted to add something, and then we'll move to something else. What did you want to say on these videos?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked for the tapes. I looked for them for a long time and persistently, and what is now being presented here is complete confusion. The recording that we saw where you ascertained that between the smoke and the explosion in the most -- in the bridge and the collapse of the bridge that there is an intervening period of a couple of minutes. That footage was recorded by an English soldier, and according to the statement that I quote in my book, he took the tape to Sarajevo under BH Army military police escort with a promise that it would be broadcast in Sarajevo, and then he boarded a plane and he left. He edited it, cut it short, and it was broadcast on BBC and other channels, and then it was picked up again. The Croatian TV did not record any footage down there. What Mr. Saric is talking about is a compilation of another tape that was recorded by a Muslim, and it's -- the quality's much worse because it's -- it's been re-taped and re-taped and re-taped. It's a copy of a copy of a copy. The footage that we saw, in accordance with the very specific statement by the BH Army was done by an English soldier whose nickname was Shote [phoen]. I know his name, because I asked German journalist who was investigating the destruction of the Old Bridge to get in touch with him, and everything was said and done. I can give you very specific information as to who recorded the first tape and who recorded the second tape, and what was taken over by specific TV channels. The Croatian TV did not record any footage down there, there were two cameras recording down there, but this is a complete mess and confusion and it's all incorrect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Your position is noted down. It's on the transcript. You're saying that you challenge the fact that this is footage from Croatian television. According to you, this was shot by a British soldier. You actually give us his name, and you know this through a German reporter who told you so. It's on the transcript. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] An even more important piece of information: It was published in Oslobodjenje newspaper. It was a press release by the BH Army specifying how this man recorded this footage, you how he reached Sarajevo under military police escort and did not allow the Sarajevo TV to broadcast it but took it on a plane and then broadcasted it on some other channel, and this is all in my book, the date of the press release and where it was published and the wording of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, Praljak, let's now move to additional questions, but I believe that my fellow Judge would like the floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Yes, Mr. Praljak, I'm a bit confused because it seems to me not so long ago this afternoon you told us that one of the videos was not known to you, available to you for the expert opinion of -- of your expert, and now you tell us that you have known everything and put it all in your book. I seem to denote a certain contradiction. Probably I misunderstood something. I would be grateful if you could explain.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Gladly, Your Honour Judge Trechsel. I'm talking about the videotape that we saw yesterday, and the one that His Honour Judge Antonetti was taking about, and that's with a great degree of probability, having some knowledge of the job, the English soldier that recorded the footage took it, and it was broadcast, Your Honour Judge Trechsel, on public TV channels, but the only thing is that a piece was cut out between the water fountain and the collapse of the bridge. Why? Because no big TV house wants to devote two minutes of it -- of its time to such an event. And this edited tape, the tape that was publicly broadcast, was at my disposal -- or, rather, the expert had it at his disposal. He also had another tape, a tape that was taken by a witness, a Muslim. We also have it here. What the expert did not have is the two minutes, or I don't know how long it is, the intervening two minutes between the water fountain and the collapse of the bridge. That part was not broadcast on any public TV. So now I'm asking the question this tape that came here, that's the original, that was not broadcast on TV, and it reached this place through some different channels, and those channels are rather problematic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. You've absolutely answered my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. General Praljak, as of next week you will no longer be a witness. Your testimony will be over. Normally it should be over Thursday after Mr. Kovacic puts some redirect to you. However, I have a few questions for you, and after that I'll no longer have the opportunity to put these questions to you, so I'll do it now. I want to put questions to you on maps. We'll come back to this in a minute, but I have a technical question first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm using this opportunity to put this question to you right now. I read very carefully the report you made by the expert that you share with Mr. Petkovic, Mr. Gorjanc - excuse me for not pronouncing his name correctly - and we'll be hearing this expert witness during the Petkovic case but it's an expert that you share with the Petkovic Defence. I was looking at all the documents used to back this expert's report. There's three whole volumes of documents, and I found a document that was -- brought a question to me. It's 3D2591. I believe that it's been downloaded -- or uploaded, so we can probably see it on the screen. 3D2591, please. We have it here on the screen. It's an interim report coming from the Electronic Operations Centre of the HVO Main Staff, and it's dated September 21, 1993, which is a time where you were commander of the HVO. When you were commander of the HVO, were you aware of the existence of this department that was tapping conversations or tapping radio conversations or telephone conversations? Here obviously are these radio conversations that are tapped. Were you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did know, Judge Antonetti, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Here -- I won't go into details -- but here it's a conversation between Zuka and Alija Izetbegovic that was tapped. However, what -- Izetbegovic's words are not tapped because they don't have the transmission frequency used by Izetbegovic. So -- however, they were able to record Zuka's words. Therefore, you're telling us that the HVO was able, technically, to eavesdrop on conversations. At your command level were you able to use all this to get information on what the enemy was about to do, BiH Army, for example, or possibly the VRS?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were possibilities for a certain number of intercepts of conversations, not all of them. Some were protected, unfortunately or by chance. The BH Army, because it had more money, it had better devices for communication, more than the HVO, and the document that I showed was introduced with permission from the HVO. Jasmin Jaganjac has a whole set of documents to that effect, but we did have certain -- a certain amount of success in intercepting certain conversations and, of course, that information from VOS, V-O-S, and Mr. Keza who was head of VOS attached to the Main Staff, I would receive -- I received information, and I can say that that information was relatively -- relatively good and correct.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your answer. I would now like to turn to the maps. The last document that was shown by the Prosecutor, P11033 fully warrants the need to have before us maps showing the position of different military units. In the documents that were established in Vinkovci by Kapular, we have seen that soldiers from the 4th Motorised Brigade are unwilling to go to the south front of the Croatian republic. What is this, a flank? Precisely. Maybe with the aid of maps we will be able to see later on what exactly this means. During cross-examination we saw several documents such that I believed it would be useful to have maps to better understand. Notwithstanding this, re-reading the indictment and the pre-trial brief, there are many references to military positions. Just to give one example, in paragraph 18 of the pre-trial brief it is stated that in September 1991, Croatia was at war with the nationalist Serb forces, and this begs the question as to where the belligerent parties were positioned. In paragraph 28, the Prosecutor talks about the first bouts of fighting in Travnik and Prozor. So here again, it would be very worthwhile to know exactly where the forces were positioned. In paragraph 33 of said brief, the Prosecutor says that in April there was a deadline set for April 15th, that thereafter military operations were conducted, and from April 16th to April 18th of 1993 there were 30 attacks launched against towns and villages, and OTP says that in Ahmici on April 30th, Sovici, Doljani on April 17th, Parcani, Lizoperci and Toscanica - and I do apologise for my pronunciation - from April 17th to 19th. Altogether, 30 towns and villages that were attacked. So it would be very useful to see this on a map. The Prosecutor in paragraph 35 says that on May 9th and 10th the HVO and Herceg-Bosna forces attacked Bosnian monuments in Mostar, and the OTP goes on to say that as early as June of 1993, Herceg-Bosna forces and HVO forces started -- or laid siege to Mostar East and that the siege lasted until April 1994. This would be indicated in paragraph 34. In paragraph 36, OTP then goes on to say that following an attack of the BiH against an HVO camp in a northern part of Mostar, and here we discover that such attacks take place as is written by the Prosecutor, so here again, it would be very useful to see where the BiH was positioned at the time of this attack. Maybe we will get an answer to this question later on. In paragraph 37 OTP states that in early July Herceg-Bosna's forces, either with the support and the participation of the government and the armed forces of the republic, the Croatian republic, launched a large scale campaign that was aimed at attacking, arresting, and detaining Bosnian Muslims. That's paragraph 37. Then OTP continues in paragraph 38, and here I'm quoting directly: "The HVO and Herceg-Bosna operations were taking place according to the following lines. Muslim were is arrested, then attacks are launched against the towns and villages. This is the modus operandi." All of this is in paragraph 38. Reading this and based on all the exhibits we have seen so far, I raise the question, the following question: For our better understanding, it would be useful to have maps in order to visualise all of the events I just referred to. This is why I have asked you to prepare maps for us that would show us the positioning of the JNA in 1991, 1992, and 1993, to see exactly where the JNA positions were. Secondly, to see when there is a conflict between the JNA and the Croatian republic where the fighting takes place. You have many times referred to Dubrovnik, so it would be very interesting and worthwhile to see what took place. And I would like to see again on the basis of your maps how over time from 1992, in October in Prozor, where was HVO and where was the BH Army. And then up until January through April, June, and November, what was respect -- what were the respective positions of HVO and the BH Army. So I'm saying starting with ELMO, what were the respective positions? I cannot contest or challenge the fact that the VRS was present or the BH Army was there or the HVO was there. All of this will be thoroughly checked and counter-checked with other -- or against other exhibits. I'm just asking you to the best of your knowledge to give us the respective positions of the armed forces and presence. If you're able to do this quickly this should expedite matters. We need to put ELMO en route, and then you can just simply say to us, This is map number 1, this is map number 2. Identify your maps. I'm just asking you to assist us in visualising things. I am asking the registrar to start ELMO so we can visualise the map. General, please explain what is this map.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This map depicts the attack by the Yugoslav People's Army and the Army of Republika Srpska which was in its initial stages of development at the time, and here on Mostar, the south of Croatia up to this area -- well, we didn't go further when we did this map. So the JNA and the reservists took the eastern bank of the Neretva River, Stolac, and all the dominant heights around Mostar, and they wanted to attack further on. They attacked Livno, Kupres, and on the 10th of April they managed to take it. They attacked on -- they attacked Livno on the 23rd of April, and the attack was repelled. And on the 15th of May they managed to expel all the population from East Mostar. They tore down all the bridges apart from the Old Bridge after that. And that was the situation in this area at that point in time. So that's map number 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Please move to map 2.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This map shows -- I'm receiving an echo. Is somebody's microphone on or ... This map shows the joint action by the Croatian Defence Council and BH Army from the 10th of April, 1992, to the 7th of June, 1992. Therefore, the blue is the HVO, the green is the BH Army, the red is the Yugoslav People's Army of Republika Srpska. Up until that time, the Army of Republika Srpska had taken control of 70 per cent of the territory in this area here, and facing the -- the Army of Republika Srpska are the HVO units. Here you have the BH Army units. I have too much volume here, an echo. My voice is coming back to me, an echo. I can hear myself speak.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's something wrong with the B/C/S channel, because we have a lot of interruption on the channel, a lot of noise, and it's unpleasant to listen to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. There must be a technical problem. This is for registrar. Please, General, try to carry on.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this area here, this area was defended by the BH Army. Sarajevo was defended by the BH Army with the proviso that this area here, facing Kiseljak, was the HVO in relation to the Army of Republika Srpska. This area here around Tuzla mostly was defended by the joint units of the BH Army and HVO according to their positions. The area -- I think this is Gradacac or Zepa. Anyway, this area was defended by the BH Army, and so was this area here. The Serbs were on the attack towards Posavina over here. We'll see that on the next map. And here I omitted Bihac. And you'll see all this on the next map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Map 3, please.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Map number 3, once again the blue is the HVO. I don't want to repeat this. It is the joint activities of the HVO and the BH Army from June to the 29th of October, 1992. Bihac was defended by far more significant BH Army forces. That is to say, there were more BH Army units and soldiers, but there were also the HVO. The Serbian army was launching a fierce attack on Posavina in order to gain a corridor for supplies. These two enclaves are under a siege, have been encircled. The HVO, together with the help of a weak BH Army at that time, managed to liberate the eastern and then western part of Mostar, too, the whole of Stolac and the Neretva River valley. Here towards Konjic you had the BH Army, then some small forces of the HVO, then the BH Army defending this area here -- or, rather, the HVO forces under the command of the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, just to make sure, it seems to me that the -- I have difficulties in seeing the difference -- the only difference between those two maps is that in number 3 we have Bihac that was omitted in number 2 and we have these red flashes. Is that correct, that's the only difference?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I can't work like this. I can't hear myself speak, Judge Trechsel. Could this be put right? Could the technician put this right? There is an essential difference between these two maps because strong attacks on Jajce are going on, and the Army of Republika Srpska is launching fierce attacks and taking control of this area defended by the HVO. And we also have a difference here in map number 3. During that period of time we liberated -- well, the HVO, with the help of the BH Army and the Muslims who were in the HVO, we managed to liberate this entire area, Mostar, Stolac, and the Neretva River valley.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This map is similar to the previous map. Number? Yes. It's number 4, map number 4. Jajce had fallen. There was no more Jajce. And the Army of Republika Srpska took control of Bosanski Brod and the other places, and only a small enclave was left to the end of the war which the HVO managed to keep. So the fall of Jajce, the fall of Bosanska Posavina except for that small enclave there, and that was on the 29th of October, 1992. This was the situation then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Regarding map number 4, October 29th, 1992, this is an important date. We can make a connection between this and the events that took place in Prozor. I see, however that, the VRS is indicated in red and it is facing off with the HVO and the BH Army acting jointly. So they have a common front line opposing them to the VRS. That is correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, Judge Antonetti. And in Bihac, and in Sarajevo are units there, and as has been marked in here. They held the front jointly facing the VRS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, a very quick question. Let us look at the map. If the HVO were to withdraw from its positions, would this mean that the VRS would be able to take the Bihac in a pincer movement and occupy all of the territory?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. Completely correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very good. Please move to the next map.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Map number 5 shows the ratio in 1993. At the time there was a conflict in Uskoplje the 11th to the 23rd of January and a BH Army attack, Busovaca-Kiseljak. This problem was dealt with. There was a truce in Uskoplje. However, the BH Army managed to cut across this area here where the HVO was linked up, and so part of Busovaca was cut off from part of Kiseljak. The other lines were held as if nothing was going on. As far as the Tuzla region is concerned, the BH Army and the HVO. Then here you had the HVO, then down here above Mostar the HVO, then the BH Army towards Konjic, and towards Tomislavgrad and Livno you had the HVO. In the area here of Bugojno, joint forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Another quick question. In January, according to your maps, and here I'm asking the question -- I'm putting the question to you, two military actions are underway. One is in Gornji Vakuf, the other one in Busovaca, Kiseljak. These are the two military operations took place in January. This is what you have indicated on your map.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to you, the actions in Gornji Vakuf were carried out by the BH Army, and Kiseljak and Busovaca is also carried out by the BH Army? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. The BH Army and Uskoplje placed the HVO in an illogical position but unfortunately they didn't want to come up to the positions facing the Army of Republika Srpska which were located over here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us move to the next map.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I apologise for the interruption. At some point the Prosecution wants to make some sort of a response. I don't what. We heard about Gornji Vakuf at length on direct. We heard about Gornji Vakuf by other Defence, I believe. We did it on cross, and here we are now providing a forum again to cover this territory, for the General to make assertions at a point when we've pretty much finished examining the witness.
